:::{#def-differentiable-on}
#### Differentiable on an interval

A function $f$ is **differentiable on** an interval
if it is differentiable (@def-differentiable) at every point of the interval
other than its [endpoints](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/sets.html#def-interval),
and, at each endpoint that belongs to the interval,
it has the one-sided derivative (@def-one-sided-derivative) from inside the interval:
the right-hand derivative at the left endpoint
and the left-hand derivative at the right endpoint.

[@larsonCalc11e, Section 2.1, p. 100]

:::
